    "title": "New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations",
    "body": "Adding an abstract order() method to the public CryptoProvider interface is binary and source incompatible for any external implementation compiled against an older Keycloak version. During CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, sorting calls order() on every loaded provider, so an older implementation will fail with AbstractMethodError even if it is the only provider on the classpath. Provide a default implementation such as default int order() { return 0; } or preserve SPI compatibility."
  },

    "category": "security",
    "title": "Providers with equal order are selected silently and arbitrarily",
    "body": "The new logic replaces the previous fail-fast multiple-provider check with sorting by order(). But all built-in providers except AuthzClientCryptoProvider (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) return 200. If two of them end up on the classpath, the selection depends on ServiceLoader encounter order and no error is raised. This can silently select the non-FIPS provider in a FIPS-required environment, or vice versa, defeating the old classpath integrity guard. Distinct orders are needed for each real provider, or a tie at the top order should still fail."
  },

    "title": "getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle",
    "body": "KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() returns the JCA provider backing the default keystore type (usually SUN/SunJCE on a stock JDK), not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers of CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() may check for null or use the returned provider to request BC-specific algorithms, so this can lead to NoSuchAlgorithmException or use of an unintended security provider. If this provider intentionally does not use BouncyCastle, it should return null or a provider that actually supplies the algorithms it claims to support, and callers must handle that."
  },

    "file": "authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java",
    "line": 134,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Indefinite BER length leaks into DER parser and causes unchecked exception",
    "body": "readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). readInteger() then passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[length] and throws unchecked NegativeArraySizeException rather than the declared IOException. A malformed DER signature can therefore bypass normal error handling. This DER decoder should reject indefinite-length encoding explicitly, and readInteger() should also reject an empty INTEGER before new BigInteger(bytes) to avoid NumberFormatException."
  },

    "body": "The test computes rsConcat from the JCA DER signature, converts it back to asn1Des, then only asserts that converting asn1Des back to raw gives the same rsConcat. A paired defect in asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER could pass this roundtrip while still producing the wrong raw signature from the original DER, or the wrong DER from the raw signature. It should also assert that asn1Des equals the original sign, or compare against known DER/raw vectors."

findings.title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Adding an abstract order() method to the public CryptoProvider interface is binary and source incompatible for any external implementation compiled against an older Keycloak version. During CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, sorting calls order() on every loaded provider, so an older implementation will fail with AbstractMethodError even if it is the only provider on the classpath. Provide a default implementation such as default int order() { return 0; } or preserve SPI compatibility.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are selected silently and arbitrarily
findings.body: The new logic replaces the previous fail-fast multiple-provider check with sorting by order(). But all built-in providers except AuthzClientCryptoProvider (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) return 200. If two of them end up on the classpath, the selection depends on ServiceLoader encounter order and no error is raised. This can silently select the non-FIPS provider in a FIPS-required environment, or vice versa, defeating the old classpath integrity guard. Distinct orders are needed for each real provider, or a tie at the top order should still fail.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() returns the JCA provider backing the default keystore type (usually SUN/SunJCE on a stock JDK), not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers of CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() may check for null or use the returned provider to request BC-specific algorithms, so this can lead to NoSuchAlgorithmException or use of an unintended security provider. If this provider intentionally does not use BouncyCastle, it should return null or a provider that actually supplies the algorithms it claims to support, and callers must handle that.

findings.title: Indefinite BER length leaks into DER parser and causes unchecked exception
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). readInteger() then passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[length] and throws unchecked NegativeArraySizeException rather than the declared IOException. A malformed DER signature can therefore bypass normal error handling. This DER decoder should reject indefinite-length encoding explicitly, and readInteger() should also reject an empty INTEGER before new BigInteger(bytes) to avoid NumberFormatException.

findings.title: Test does not verify the first DER-to-raw conversion against the original signature
findings.body: The test computes rsConcat from the JCA DER signature, converts it back to asn1Des, then only asserts that converting asn1Des back to raw gives the same rsConcat. A paired defect in asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER could pass this roundtrip while still producing the wrong raw signature from the original DER, or the wrong DER from the raw signature. It should also assert that asn1Des equals the original sign, or compare against known DER/raw vectors.
